input.summary: Full ledger built and traced. All 20 claims (independent 1, 11, 16 plus dependents 2-10, 12-15, 17-20) were traced limitation by limitation to affirmative inventor text: rigid base with first/second sides, vibration motor coupled to the first side, air-extraction mechanism (vacuum pump) coupled to the first side and in fluid communication with a chamber on the second side, rigid low-friction loop/skirt of plastic, metal, PTFE or a combination of rigid materials, non-sealing perimeter admitting air "beneath the rigid perimeter" (drafted as the clearance along at least part), continuous extraction maintaining the chamber below atmospheric pressure, pressure-differential hold with no operator downforce, an all-rigid motor-to-tile path with substantially less damping than a flexible suction cup, sliding to successive areas while the hold is maintained, guiding handles, the rope/wire/cable pulling element with decoupled control, and stirring elements for autonomous constant forward motion (the only conversation USER passage carrying technical substance; all other USER turns are operational resume/repair instructions and were treated as non-authority). All 17 numerals (10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 34, 36, 38, 40, 42, 44, 46, 48) were checked for single meaning, presence in the numerals table, use in the description, and appearance in at least one figure; every "Numerals appearing on this figure" list matches the identified parts in that brief and the numerals table. All six figure briefs (FIGS. 1-6) and the Brief Description of the Drawings were compared item by item: schematic recitals, omitted parts (motor/handle in FIG. 2; motor/extraction mechanism in FIG. 5; covering element in FIG. 6) and sectioned bodies agree between text and brief, and the section designations 2-2 and 4-4 use the same repeated designation in FIG. 3's brief, in the FIG. 2 and FIG. 4 view lines, and in the drawing description. Depiction choices that the sources do not fix - rectangular plan form, ring width, band and leg depth, slab thickness, block order and spacing, handle form/size/mounting, the schematic communication gap through the slab, the flat lower end of the perimeter member, the pulling-element meeting place, and the number/position of the stirring elements - are each confined to their figure brief and expressly marked as conventions with no port, duct, valve, attachment formation, engagement, contact extent or bearing-face shape asserted; no functional-surface statement about depth ordering, circumferential or radial end position, runout, taper, angle or contact topology was verbalized anywhere. No application text (Field, Summary, Brief Description, Detailed Description, claims, abstract) broadens an embodiment or adds "by way of example"/"any closed outline" language to justify a rendering choice; the words "rectangular" and similar shape terms appear only inside the figure briefs. Internal checks passed: claim antecedent basis in claims 1, 11 and 16 and their dependents; identical relationships and terms between claims, summary and detailed description; prior-art "sliding base" kept lexically distinct from the claimed base 12; abstract at about 145 words; title, "Not applicable." cross-reference and government-support sections matching the filing brief; and no drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction, unresolved alternative or internal comment remaining in any section or brief. Background prior-art characterizations were not treated as requiring inventor support. No unsupported or inconsistent passage was found.
